answer: In a decentralized agent network, Sybil resistance relies on costly identity formation and stake-backed proofs. Each agent must bind a unique cryptographic key to a jetty of stake, raising the marginal cost of fake replicas. Consensus rewards are capped at the zenith of rational participation, so a fork or duplicate must exceed that threshold to profit. If a replica misbehaves, slashing moves its reputation to a harbor of penalties, making negative expected utility inevitable.
